title: Patch lane sandbox deploy notes
content:
Objective: Quick, low-risk patch to prod-sandbox pool (patch-lane) to roll out kernel/optimizer improvements and a small routing change. Goal: validate routing fallback and latency SLO impact under synthetic load. This is intentionally conservative: small traffic window, aggressive telemetry sampling, and pre-defined rollback.

Summary notes (working):
- Patch contains: optimizer v2.1.3 (kernel selection tweak), routing config flag enable_fallback=true, and a minor health-check timeout tweak for grpc-agent.
- Target pool: prod-sandbox (not customer-facing but mirrors prod topology).
- Release window: 2026-08-20 01:00–05:00 UTC (maintenance window).
- Expected risk: low. Primary risk vector: cache key compatibility during optimizer switch (may cause transient CPU spike).
- Rollback plan: immediate configuration revert + scale-up older runtime container if anomaly threshold crossed.

Owners & contacts:
- Release lead: Elena Park (pager: elena@redwood.ai, slack: @elena)
- Deploy engineer: Marcus Li (slack: @marcus)
- Observability lead: Priya Nair (slack: @priya)
- SRE escalation: Omar Rodriguez (on-call pager)
- Runtime SME: Jae Kim (github PR reviewer)
- Incident commander alternate: @infra-ic (channel #infra-ic)

Preflight checklist (must be green before any traffic shift):
[ ] Code review merged: PR #1287 (platform) — verified by Jae
[ ] Canary image built and pinned: registry.redwood.ai/platform:opt-v2.1.3-canary
[ ] Nightly smoke run against canary image: success (see test logs)
[ ] Telemetry dashboards for patch-lane forked and baseline recorded (last 7 days median)
[ ] Backfill plan confirmed (if we need to run fallback): extra capacity reserved + autoscale policy tested
[ ] Stakeholders notified: #release-notices, #customer-success (FYI)
[ ] Postmortem template pre-created in Confluence (link in linked_artifacts)

Calendar (UTC):
- 2026-08-19 16:00 — Dry run in staging (Marcus) — simulate load and verify KV cache behavior
- 2026-08-20 00:00 — Final preflight check (all owners) — last green check required
- 2026-08-20 01:00 — Deploy canary (5% traffic to patch-lane) — automation: deploy-runner v4.3
- 2026-08-20 01:30 — Observe metrics; hold for 30m if no regressions
- 2026-08-20 02:00 — Expand to 30% for 60m (if OK)
- 2026-08-20 03:00 — Expand to 70% for 30m (if OK)
- 2026-08-20 03:30 — Full cutover to patch-lane (100%) or abort/rollback if thresholds hit
- 2026-08-20 04:30 — Stabilization window; begin post-release checks and perf sampling
- 2026-08-20 05:00 — Close and handoff to ops shift; post-deploy notes consolidated

Automated gating thresholds (if any threshold crossed -> immediate rollback):
- 5xx error rate > 0.2% sustained over 2m
- Median p95 latency increase > 20% vs baseline over 5m
- CPU utilization on runtime nodes > 85% for 5m
- KV cache miss rate spike > 3x baseline for 10m

Deploy steps (quick runbook):
1) Tag and push canary image: registry tag done by CI (Marcus).
2) Update routing config in config-store (enable_fallback=true) in canary namespace only.
3) Trigger deploy-runner to rollout canary to 5% with autoscaling disabled for first 20m.
4) Run synthetic load (traffic-replayer) to generate realistic token distribution for 10 minutes.
5) Observability: Priya runs smoke script and checks the dashboards (latency, error rates, CPU, cache miss).
6) If green -> proceed per calendar; if any gating crossed -> rollback per rollback steps below.

Smoke & verification checklist (first 30m):
[ ] API surface sanity (text generation + embeddings) under 95th percentile latency check
[ ] Trace sampling verifies kernel v2.1.3 in request path (confirm via trace tag: kernel=opt-v2.1.3)
[ ] Function-calling tests (tooling) succeed end-to-end at 100 requests per second baseline
[ ] KV cache warm-up completes within expected timeframe (< 5m after first 1k requests)
[ ] No increased 5xx in upstream connectors (auth, datastore)

Telemetry sampling plan (explicit):
- Full trace sampling at 100% for canary instances for first 45m (high fidelity)
- Metric retention: increased resolution for 6 hours (1s granularity to detect microspikes)
- Log sampling: 100% logs for canary pods for 2 hours, then 10% afterwards
- Create ephemeral alert room: #deploy-patch-lane-2026-08-20 (auto-created)

Rollback matrix (fast paths):
- Immediate revert: set routing back to previous config and scale back canary deployment -> expected RTO: ~3m
- Cold rollback (if image bug): deploy previous stable image to patch-lane and gradually shift traffic -> RTO ~10–20m
- Fallback to regional pool: route traffic to nearest fallback pool (regional) while we investigate -> RTO 8–12m (requires approval by infra-ic)

Post-deploy checks (to be completed before handoff):
[ ] Telemetry sanity pass (no residual spikes in next 30m)
[ ] Post-deploy smoke suite run (all tests pass)
[ ] Pager checks: no new P0/P1 incidents in 2h after cutover
[ ] Rollout notes written and posted to #release-notes thread (Elena)
[ ] Postmortem owner assigned if any gating threshold triggered or if rollback occurred

Known risks & mitigations:
- Risk: transient higher CPU due to optimizer re-jit. Mitigation: keep canary low and enable high-res telemetry; pre-reserve spare nodes for rapid scale-up.
- Risk: cache key incompatibility. Mitigation: dry-run in staging with synthetic KV patterns; have fallback to immutable runtime that uses old cache semantics.
- Risk: alert fatigue from increased trace sampling. Mitigation: temporary alert muting for non-critical noise (Priya to tune alerts).

Open questions (tracked):
- Do we want longer canary (90m) given kernel changes? Action: decision by 2026-08-19 23:00 UTC.
- Should we add an explicit canary tag to logs for easier log-grep? (Jae to comment)
- Are we comfortable with 100% trace sampling for 45m cost? Finance gave FYI but want post-deploy cost snapshot.

Quick stash of commands (for deploy engineer):
- deploy-runner rollout --pool prod-sandbox --image registry.redwood.ai/platform:opt-v2.1.3-canary --traffic 5%
- telemetryctl sampling set --pool prod-sandbox --traces 100% --duration 45m
- config-store set routing/patch-lane/enable_fallback true --namespace canary

After-action notes template (to fill within 24h):
- Summary: one-paragraph summary of what happened.
- Metrics: p95 latency, 5xx delta, CPU spike windows, KV miss rate.
- Rollout decisions and rationale.
- Any unexpected issues and root cause (if known).
- Action items and owners (with due dates).

Appendix / links: PR #1287, RLSE-3421 (backfill plan), Confluence: Patch lane overview (linked above).

Scratchpad / quick thoughts (notes to self):
- If we see KV miss rate spike -> consider temporary throttle on long-tail requests (elastic throttle) before rolling back to reduce noise.
- Keep a close eye on ingress auth latencies; recent infra change might correlate.
- If rollback happens, prioritize postmortem and a safe plan to re-introduce optimizer change in smaller increments.
